# `/skill:craft-parley`

This skill covers:

- [What you produce](#what-you-produce): the document, the review page and the answers file.
- [The loop](#the-loop): check, serve, listen, hand over the link, reply, new round or render.
- [Blocks](#blocks): which block type shows what. `writing.md` has sources and questions.
- [Revising](writing.md#revising): what to change between rounds.
- [Reference](#reference): the files beside this one, and when to read each.

## What you produce

You write a document, `docs/parley/<id>.json`. Parley turns it into a review page. The reviewer
reads it, comments on any item, answers your questions and gives a verdict. Their words land in
`docs/parley/<id>.answers.json`, and you reply into it.

Use parley when a person must review something with you and their answers change what you do
next: a design, a schema, a migration, a diff, a plan. A document with no questions is an
explanatory document: the reviewer reads it and finishes.

A document is any mix of blocks, in any order, down to one `prose` block.
`node parley.mjs schema document --md` prints the smallest valid document.

`/skill:craft-explain` and `/skill:craft-discuss` write documents for their own subjects.

`parley.mjs` sits in this skill's folder. Run it from the project root, as
`node <this folder>/parley.mjs <command>`; the commands below write it `node parley.mjs`. `bun` and
`deno run -A` work the same as `node`. `node parley.mjs <command> --help` lists a command's flags.

## The loop

Read `loop.md` before the first step. Each step links its rules there.

1. [Check](loop.md#check): `node parley.mjs check <doc.json>`; fix what it prints, warnings too.
2. [Serve](loop.md#serve): `node parley.mjs serve [dir]` in the background, left running. The page
   opens any tracked file; share a `--host 0.0.0.0` token link only with repo readers.
3. [Listen](loop.md#listen): `node parley.mjs answers <id> [dir] --wait` as a background command.
   Don't poll, and don't hand the wait to a subagent.
4. [Hand over the link](loop.md#hand-over-the-link): only once a listener runs.
5. [Reply to each send](loop.md#reply-to-each-send): `--reply <thread id>`, then listen again.
   Every send stays pending until you reply.
6. [New round or render](loop.md#new-round-or-render): on `[verdict]`, revise
   ([writing.md](writing.md#revising)) or render.

## Blocks

Each block has an `id`, a `type` and an optional `title`. Every item inside has an `id` too. Ids
are unique across the document. Before you write a block, run
`node parley.mjs schema <type> --md`. It prints the block's fields, what the page shows and a
passing example. `schema --md` lists the parts, such as `questions` and `source`, and every block
type. `writing.md` has the rules for sources, questions and revising.

| To show | Use |
|---|---|
| Paragraphs of explanation, or a whole narrative | `prose` |
| One image or video with a caption | `figure` |
| Live Storybook stories and screenshots side by side | `story` |
| A question at its place in the reading | `question` |
| A query, config or text with numbered notes on parts of it | `annotated-text` |
| Tables, columns, keys and relations | `schema` |
| Ordered changes with risk, locks and rollback | `operations` |
| A grid of rows by columns, each cell valid, warn, error or skip | `matrix` |
| One request walked through ordered candidates | `trace` |
| A ladder of rules where the first match wins | `precedence` |
| Phases, workstreams and tasks | `plan` |
| One path through code across files, as a sequence diagram | `code-flow` |
| A process with lanes and decisions, as a flowchart | `workflow` |
| A diff with review findings on its lines | `diff` |
| Numbers per column, the change and which way is better | `metrics` |
| A question's options scored against weighted criteria | `tradeoffs` |

## Reference

These files sit beside this one. Each line says when to read it.

- `loop.md`: the rules for each loop step. Read it before the first step.
- `writing.md`: sources, questions and revising. Read it before you write a question or revise.
- `answers.md`: what the page shows, what reaches you and when, and the answers file. Read it
  when a send or the answers file is unclear.
- `glossary.md`: the one name for each parley idea. Read it before you name one in prose.
- `examples/`: whole documents that pass `check`, in folders by subject. Start from the closest.
